examples.question_text: A rectangle has area $54$ m$^{2}$. Its length is $3$ m more than its breadth. Find its dimensions.
A triangle has area $28$ cm$^{2}$. Its perpendicular height is $1$ cm less than its base. Find its base and height.
The product of two consecutive positive integers is $110$. Find the integers.
examples.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the smaller integer. The next integer is $x+1$.
$\begin{aligned}x(x+1)&=110\\x^{2}+x-110&=0\\(x+11)(x-10)&=0\\x&=-11\ \text{or}\ 10\end{aligned}$
Reject $x=-11$ because the integers are positive. The integers are $10$ and $11$.

examples.question_text: When a positive integer is increased by $20$, the result is $10$ less than its square. Find the integer.
examples.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the integer.
$\begin{aligned}x+20&=x^{2}-10\\x^{2}-x-30&=0\\(x-6)(x+5)&=0\\x&=6\ \text{or}\ -5\end{aligned}$
Reject $x=-5$ because the integer is positive. The integer is $6$.

examples.question_text: Two positive numbers differ by $4$. The sum of their squares is $136$. Find the numbers.
examples.solution_text:
Let $x$ be the smaller number. The larger number is $x+4$.
$\begin{aligned}x^{2}+(x+4)^{2}&=136\\2x^{2}+8x+16&=136\\2x^{2}+8x-120&=0\\x^{2}+4x-60&=0\\(x+10)(x-6)&=0\\x&=-10\ \text{or}\ 6\end{aligned}$
Reject $x=-10$ because both numbers must be positive. The numbers are $6$ and $10$.

examples.question_text: Three consecutive positive odd integers have this property: the product of the first and third is $11$ less than $8$ times the middle integer. Find the integers.
examples.solution_text:
Let the integers be $x$, $x+2$ and $x+4$.
$\begin{aligned}x(x+4)&=8(x+2)-11\\x^{2}+4x&=8x+5\\x^{2}-4x-5&=0\\(x-5)(x+1)&=0\\x-5&=0\ \text{or}\ x+1=0\\x&=5\ \text{or}\ -1\end{aligned}$
Reject $x=-1$ because all three integers must be positive. The integers are $5$, $7$ and $9$.
Check: $5\times9=45$ and $8\times7-11=45$.

examples.question_text: A ball's height $h$ metres after $t$ seconds is $h=t(10-t)$. Find the times when its height is $21$ m.
examples.solution_text:
$\begin{aligned}t(10-t)&=21\\10t-t^{2}&=21\\t^{2}-10t+21&=0\\(t-3)(t-7)&=0\\t&=3\ \text{or}\ 7\end{aligned}$
Both times lie between launch at $t=0$ and return to ground at $t=10$. The ball reaches $21$ m after $3$ s on the way up and after $7$ s on the way down.

examples.question_text: A rectangular garden measuring $8$ m by $4$ m is surrounded by a path of uniform width. The path alone has area $64$ m$^{2}$. Find its width.
A rectangle has perimeter $34$ cm and area $60$ cm$^{2}$. Find its dimensions.
examples.solution_text:
Let one side be $x$ centimetres. Half the perimeter is $17$ cm, so the other side is $17-x$ centimetres.
$\begin{aligned}x(17-x)&=60\\17x-x^{2}&=60\\x^{2}-17x+60&=0\\(x-5)(x-12)&=0\\x&=5\ \text{or}\ 12\end{aligned}$
Both roots give positive side lengths and describe the same rectangle. Its dimensions are $5$ cm by $12$ cm.

examples.question_text: A trapezium has parallel sides whose lengths differ by $4$ cm. Its perpendicular height is $2$ cm more than the shorter parallel side. Its area is $64$ cm$^{2}$. Find the shorter parallel side.
